text: A Uniswap v4 position has no stop. Getting out is a transaction, and somebody has to send it.
Ripcord arms a line once. A Reactive contract on Lasna watches every swap, and pulls your liquidity when one crosses it.
This is a real loop, live, not sped up. One call arms a line, one tick spacing from the price.
Departed. Two blocks, two seconds on Unichain's clock, from the swap to the exit.
And nothing of the owner's ran.
Its three hops, replayed at chain speed: the swap on Unichain, the reaction on Lasna, the exit.
Every departure on the board is read from chain. Fifty measured loops: all fifty exited within three seconds.

Why the seconds matter: Reactive's previous version made a block every seven seconds. In the worst half hour of the October 2025 crash, ETH fell a median twenty-five basis points in seven seconds, and fifteen point seven in three.
What it refuses matters as much.
A swap that stops short of the line: Lasna still reacts, and asks for no callback.
An exit called by anyone but Reactive's callback proxy: the chain reverts it.
And when the owner has revoked approval, the ripcord still pulls, but the vault records a refusal on-chain instead of touching the position.
Testnet only, not audited. Your Uniswap v4 position leaves the pool within three seconds of crossing your line, with nothing of yours running.
